{"message":"Hi! Meridian caps each webhook payload at a fixed size. If a record’s full content would exceed that limit, the webhook sends only an `id` with `truncated: true` instead of the full data. Your consumer should treat that flag as a signal to fetch the complete record via the API.

For records that are often large, we recommend subscribing to the `.changed` event and retrieving the current record by ID yourself—this bypasses the payload size cap entirely.

Also, note that webhook delivery isn’t batch‑configurable; each change is sent as its own event, so any batching must be handled on your side after you fetch the records.

Hi! Meridian caps each webhook payload at a fixed size. If a record’s full content would exceed that limit, the webhook sends only an `id` with `truncated: true` instead of the full data. Your consumer should treat that flag as a signal to fetch the complete record via the API.

For records that are often large, we recommend subscribing to the `.changed` event and retrieving the current record by ID yourself—this bypasses the payload size cap entirely.

Also, note that webhook delivery isn’t batch‑configurable; each change is sent as its own event, so any batching must be handled on your side after you fetch the records.

Let me know if you need more details on how to fetch the full record or set up the `.changed` subscription!
